text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- The Socialist Party presidium issued a statement last night accusing junior coalition partner, the Free Democrats, of trying to wriggle out of the responsibility of joint governing in the scandal surrounding the State Privatisation and Holding Co. (APV). The presidium supports the investigations aimed at clearing up the matter.

- Parliament began debate yesterday on an amendment that would authorise the tax authority to withhold the payment of tax refund if the taxpayer owes money to any of the customs authorities or social insurance organisations. @
- Employers expressed their objections to the government's proposed amendment to the social insurance payment scheme.
- Finance Ministry State Secretary Laszlo Akar threatened to sue Smallholders President Jozsef Torgyan for slander during a heated debate in Parliament.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs is on an official visit to Greece.
- Industrial production in August fell by 9.1 per cent compared to July, and by 3.2 per cent compared to a year earlier, the Central Statistics Office reported. @
- All 1.2 million pieces of BorsodChem shares were sold for HUF 2,940 through a closed offering.
- An explosion rocked the Halasztanya restaurant in Esztergom on Sunday night, causing the roof and furnishings to burn down, but causing no injuries.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Hungarian-born nuclear physicist Ede Teller is due to arrive in Budapest on Friday at the invitation of prime minister Gyula Horn. @
- Outgoing Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman blames some of the media and the Free Democrats for his sacking and issues a rallying cry to the Socialist Party in an open letter to the party.
- Shareholders of BNP-Dresdner Bank Rt., Banque Nationale de Paris and Dresdner Bank AG decided to raise the Hungarian bank's primary capital from HUF 2 billion to HUF 3.5 billion.
- The International Swimming Federation yesterday banned Hungarian Swimming Federation general secretary Jozsef Ruza from all activities related to FINA for two years.
NEPSZAVA @

- The TV programme "Objektiv" has reported that three persons and two shareholding companies withdrew cash from the bank account of Marta Tocsik, the lawyer whose HUF 804 million in fees is at the centre of the APV scandal.
- This paper reports that police mounted a search in Marta Tocsik's downtown office on Monday after sealing off the entire building.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek will be in Budapest on a one-day working visit today to sign an agreement on rail links between the two countries. @
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The liqudiator of the Northern Hungarian Chemical Works will put the company up for sale in November. The company will start producing pesticides within a few weeks.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
